title: Love of Allah
hookLine: say, if you love Allah, follow me, and Allah will love you (3:31)

cards: "If ye love Allah, follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins." That's the Qur'an, in Pickthall's translation, telling the Prophet ﷺ what to say. Read it slowly; it's built in three moves.
A condition: if you love. An action: follow me. And something coming back the other way: Allah will love you.
Love isn't left as a feeling you announce. It's tested by what you do next.

teach.b: The word is mahabbah, love. It isn't only a word for poets. It's in the Qur'an, and it runs both ways.
In Pickthall's translation of another verse, Allah will bring "a people whom He loveth and who love Him." He loves first in that line. So how does a person grow in it?
Love shows up as imitation; people who love someone pick up their habits, their words, the way they treat others.

Then there's a hadith qudsi, words the Prophet reported from Allah, in Sahih al-Bukhari, and it lays out the path step by step. My servant draws near to Me with nothing dearer to Me than what I have made obligatory.
And My servant keeps drawing near with extra deeds until I love him. And when I love him, I become the hearing he hears with, the sight he sees with, the hand he holds with, the foot he walks with.
Commentators are careful here. They warn against reading it as Allah becoming a person's body, and read it as a life so guided that the person hears, sees and acts as Allah would love.
The order matters: the duties, then the extra, then the love, then a whole life changed by it.
Love here doesn't start as a feeling you chase. It follows the steps, and then it changes the one who walks them.

how: Muslims speak of love of Allah as shown by following the Prophet's example and drawing near through required and voluntary worship, and teachers of the inward path describe it as one of the stations of the path.

o: a love poem sung at weddings across the Arab world
the warm feeling of a crowd praying side by side
mahabbah: love between Allah and His servants, both ways

s: love of Allah appears only in later poetry, not in the Qur'an
"if ye love Allah, follow me" and "a people whom He loveth and who love Him" are both Qur'an.
in the verse, love is tested by following
if ye love Allah, follow me; Allah will love you.

games.q: you want to grow in love of Allah. the hadith qudsi in al-Bukhari lays out a path. where does it start?
o: with a strong feeling of love.
with what Allah has made obligatory.
games.why: nothing is dearer to Him than the duties. then come the extra deeds, then His love, then a life changed by it.

practice: Think of the extra deeds in the hadith, the ones nobody asks for: a short prayer beyond the required ones, a kind word to someone who can't return it, picking up litter on a street that isn't yours, feeding a bird.
Choose one you could do, and let the reason be simple: not for thanks, not to feel good about yourself, just for love of the One it's for.
If you pray, hold the verse, if ye love Allah, follow me; if not, hold the plain thought: this is for love.

wordCard.voice: Mahabbah. Love: Allah's love for His servants and theirs for Him, shown by following and drawing near. Today's word.
